case.title: Disputed delivery of order ORD-1042
case.question: The customer says order ORD-1042 never arrived, but carrier tracking says it was delivered. What happened to the parcel?

hypotheses.statement: The carrier delivered the parcel to the customer's address; any loss happened after delivery.
The carrier delivered the parcel to the wrong address.
The parcel never left the warehouse.

configuration.speck: Evidence Desk as built: one Speck case carried across the stages on a temporary Speck database (the case on the page is not touched). Each stage's new records are assessed and Speck's beliefs revised; a record replaced by a later one stops counting and the beliefs that rested on it are rebuilt.
configuration.stateless: The evaluation's stateless model baseline: at each stage, one call to the same Nemotron endpoint with the question, the explanations and every visible record (its text, its facts, and "replaces …" where the source says so). It keeps nothing between stages.
configuration.labels: No pre-registered labels: this case is not an evaluation case.

visible.content: Order ORD-1042 placed by customer C-7731: 1 x espresso grinder, ship to 41 Lydiard St South, Ballarat VIC 3350. Paid AUD 389.00.
Parcel PCL-88412 for ORD-1042 packed, weighed 3.2 kg, and scanned onto carrier manifest MAN-5521 at dock 3.
Tracking PCL-88412: DELIVERED 14:02 AEDT 13 Oct. Left at front door. Driver D-219.
Customer C-7731: "Tracking says it was delivered yesterday but nothing arrived. I was home all afternoon and nobody knocked."

speck.headline: Leading, not established: The carrier delivered the parcel to the customer's address; any loss happened after delivery.

support.rationale: Order was placed and shipped to the customer's address.
Carrier tracking API confirms delivery at 14:02 AEDT on 13 Oct.

against.rationale: Customer reports no delivery despite tracking.

explanation.text: The carrier tracking API (EV-CAR-003) confirms delivery at 14:02 AEDT on 13 Oct, contradicting the customer's claim of no delivery (EV-SUP-004). The order system (EV-OMS-001) and warehouse system (EV-WMS-002) support that the parcel was shipped, ruling out H-NOT-SHIPPED. The evidence points to H-DELIVERED as the most likely explanation, but it is not firmly established due to the customer's report of no delivery.

stateless.rationale: The carrier tracking API confirms delivery at 14:02 AEDT on 13 Oct, and the warehouse system shows the parcel was scanned onto the carrier manifest. The customer's non-receipt is likely due to a delivery issue after the fact.

visible.content: Order ORD-1042 placed by customer C-7731: 1 x espresso grinder, ship to 41 Lydiard St South, Ballarat VIC 3350. Paid AUD 389.00.
Parcel PCL-88412 for ORD-1042 packed, weighed 3.2 kg, and scanned onto carrier manifest MAN-5521 at dock 3.
Tracking PCL-88412: DELIVERED 14:02 AEDT 13 Oct. Left at front door. Driver D-219.
Customer C-7731: "Tracking says it was delivered yesterday but nothing arrived. I was home all afternoon and nobody knocked."
Proof-of-delivery review for PCL-88412: delivery GPS fix recorded 380 m from the ship-to address, at 41 Lydiard St North. Delivery scan amended to 'delivered to incorrect address'.
Resident of 41 Lydiard St North called: a parcel addressed to 41 Lydiard St South arrived on 13 Oct and they are holding it for collection.

speck.headline: Leading, not established: The carrier delivered the parcel to the wrong address.

support.rationale: Delivery scan amended to 'delivered to incorrect address'.
Parcel held at 41 Lydiard St North, matching delivery address.

noLongerCounted.explanation: EV-CAR-005 replaces all of EV-CAR-003, not only the facts it restates. No record that still counts states carrier.status=delivered, carrier.driver=D-219. Its judgments no longer apply: supports H-DELIVERED; contradicts H-MISDELIVERED; contradicts H-NOT-SHIPPED.

revisions.cause: support withheld: EV-CAR-005 refutes H-DELIVERED decisively; EV-CAR-003 superseded by EV-CAR-005
dropped: EV-OMS-001 (support withheld: EV-CAR-005 refutes H-DELIVERED decisively)

explanation.text: The parcel was delivered to the wrong address, as confirmed by EV-CAR-005 and EV-SUP-006, which show the delivery occurred at 41 Lydiard St North instead of 41 Lydiard St South. EV-CAR-005 contradicts H-DELIVERED and supports H-MISDELIVERED, while EV-SUP-006 confirms the resident is holding the parcel. H-DELIVERED and H-NOT-SHIPPED are ruled out by these records. The conclusion is that H-MISDELIVERED is the most likely explanation, but it is not yet established as definitive.

stateless.rationale: The carrier tracking API shows the parcel was delivered to the front door, and the proof-of-delivery review confirms a GPS fix 380m from the address, indicating delivery occurred.

notes: Both approaches saw the same records at every stage, the same question and explanations, and the same assessor configuration.

Speck counts a conclusion only when it holds it as supported; a leading or pointed-to explanation is tentative. The stateless baseline has no such threshold beyond answering "unresolved" (model) or a tie or non-positive score (rules).

Differences come from Speck's explicit evidence and revision state and its conclusion policy (thresholds, decisive refutation, supersession), not from persistence alone: the evaluation's speck-fresh system, which rebuilds from scratch each time, reaches the same conclusions as speck-desk.

Live: model judgments vary between runs. This is one sample, not a rate. Speck calls the model per evidence chunk plus once for its explanation; the baseline calls it once per stage, so call counts and latency are not like for like.
Speck caps model-judged evidence at reliability 0.4, so live Speck conclusions tend to stay tentative.
